findings.item: A peer offers to sell you leaked ISC2 exam questions, and you decline and report it
buckets_in_tension: Canon II — act honourably, honestly, justly, responsibly and legally
Canon IV — advance and protect the profession
findings.why: ISC2's own Canon II objectives include 'observe all contracts and agreements, express or implied' and acting legally/honestly - which squarely covers refusing trafficked exam material you are under NDA about. The conventional key is Canon IV (protecting the value of the credential/profession). Both are textually supported by the published canon guidance, and the stem gives no signal which frame is wanted; 'decline' points at II, 'report it' points at IV, and the item does both.
findings.suggested_fix: Split into two items: one that isolates the personal refusal (Canon II) and one that isolates the duty to report to ISC2 to protect the credential's value (Canon IV), or add an explicit cue such as '...because trafficking in exam content devalues the certification for everyone'.

buckets_in_tension: Canon II — act honourably, honestly, justly, responsibly and legally
Canon III — provide diligent and competent service to principals
Canon IV — advance and protect the profession
findings.why: Canon II ('honourably, honestly, justly, responsibly and legally') is a catch-all that textually subsumes most of the other canons' scenarios: refusing to overstate an audit report is honesty (II) but also service to a principal (III); refusing FUD in a sales pitch is honesty (II) but also protecting the profession's reputation (IV). The bucket set is hierarchical, not disjoint, so scoring depends on which canon the writer considers 'primary'.
findings.suggested_fix: Instruct the candidate to pick the canon that is MOST directly implicated, and re-word the II items so the honesty is directed at a non-client, non-professional-body party (e.g. a regulator or the public) to keep II from colliding with III and IV.

findings.why: Ransomware encryption is the textbook Availability example, but unauthorised encryption is also an unauthorised modification of the stored data, which is the definition of an Integrity loss. A candidate who has been taught 'integrity = data changed without authorisation' can defend Integrity. Most well-prepared candidates will still say Availability, so this is arguable rather than fatal.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'Ransomware encrypts the file server and staff cannot open any documents' so the graded effect (loss of access) is explicit, or move it to a SELECT where both CIA properties can be credited.

findings.why: The scenario prompt asks for records 'intact and reachable' - 'intact' is an integrity requirement - while the selection rule is 'primarily protects AVAILABILITY'. That invites a careful candidate to include 'Digital signatures on lab results' (integrity) and makes 'Offline immutable backups' ambiguous, since immutability is an integrity property and only the restore capability is availability. The IN/OUT partition is therefore not clean against the stated scenario.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop 'intact' from the prompt (e.g. 'must keep patient records reachable throughout a ransomware incident') so the scenario and the selection criterion test the same property.

findings.why: All six items are the definitional exemplars printed alongside the three factors in every syllabus (iris/fingerprint, PIN/security question, smart card/authenticator app), and each maps to its bucket by plain-English meaning of know/have/are. A candidate with zero security training scores 6/6 by ordinary language, so the bank cannot distinguish a prepared learner from an unprepared one.
findings.suggested_fix: Add at least two boundary items that require the taxonomy rather than English - e.g. 'A PIN typed into a hardware token before it will display a code' (two factors), 'Keystroke-rhythm analysis while typing your password' (something you do/are), or 'A one-time code read out over the phone by the help desk'.

findings.item: You publish your incident write-ups and mentor junior analysts so the field improves
buckets_in_tension: Canon IV — advance and protect the profession
findings.why: The stem carries its own rationale clause - 'so the field improves' - which is a direct paraphrase of the bucket label 'advance and protect the profession'. The item is answerable by matching that clause to the bucket name without knowing anything about the canons.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the purpose clause: 'You publish your incident write-ups and spend Friday afternoons mentoring junior analysts.'

findings.why: Administrative controls are standardly defined as 'policies, procedures and guidelines'. An item whose text is literally 'a written incident response procedure' is selectable by matching the word 'procedure' to that definition, with no reasoning about what the control does.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the control by its content instead of its document type - e.g. 'A documented escalation path naming who declares an incident and who notifies the regulator'.
